security_spec.violation_condition: WRS.NTO and WRS.STO instructions are decoded with blockBack=true and noSpec=true but execute as pipeline NOPs in the ROB — there is no hasWRS stall state register, no wrsEvent interrupt-wakeup signal, and no mie&mip (locally-enabled pending interrupt) check. The ROB hasWFI state machine handles WFI wakeup via (mie & mip).orR, but WRS instructions never trigger equivalent stall logic. WRS passes through the CSR execution unit (CSROpType.wrs_nto/wrs_sto) without blocking commit, so the pipeline stalls only for backend dispatch latency rather than until reservation-set invalidation or a locally-enabled pending interrupt.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: Grep for 'hasWRS|wrsEvent|wrs_event|isWrsNto|isWrsSto' in Rob.scala — absence of WRS stall state machine and interrupt wakeup logic; WRS instructions only appear in decode unit (DecodeUnit.scala:254-256) and illegal/virtual instruction checks (NewCSR.scala:1501-1502, CSR.scala wrapper:472,534) but never in ROB commit-blocking logic
security_spec.summary: WRS instructions lack ROB stall state machine and mie&mip interrupt wakeup — they execute as NOPs violating Zawrs requirement to stall until reservation-set invalidation or locally-enabled pending interrupt per WFI resumption rules
